name: kubectl get

flags.description: Output format (json, yaml, kyaml, wide, name, jsonpath=..., custom-columns=...)
Show all labels as the last column
Sort by a JSONPath expression, e.g. .metadata.creationTimestamp

examples.description: List all pods in current namespace
Find pods that are not running across all namespaces
KYAML output: a stricter, less error-prone YAML style (kubectl 1.34+)

notes: Common resources: pods, services, deployments, nodes, configmaps, secrets

name: kubectl describe
notes: Shows events, conditions, and detailed state
Since kubectl 1.36, related events are shown only when describing a single object; pass --show-events to include them for multiple objects.

name: kubectl apply

flags.description: Process the directory given with -f recursively
Use server-side apply (field ownership tracked by the API server)
Delete resources no longer in the config (requires -l or --all; use with care)

examples.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
...
EOF

notes: Preferred for declarative config management
Creates or updates resources
Run 'kubectl diff -f' first to see what will change
WARNING: --prune can delete live resources that are missing from your files; always test with --dry-run=server

name: kubectl create
description: Create resources from file or stdin

flags.description: Preview without creating; combine with -o yaml to generate manifests

examples.command: kubectl create deployment myapp --image=nginx:1.27 --dry-run=client -o yaml > deployment.yaml
examples.description: Generate a manifest to edit and commit

notes: Fails if the resource already exists; use 'apply' for declarative management
For secrets and configmaps see the dedicated 'kubectl create secret' and 'kubectl create configmap' entries

name: kubectl delete

flags.description: Seconds to wait before force delete

notes: Pods managed by deployments will be recreated
WARNING: deleting a namespace deletes everything inside it
--force --grace-period=0 skips graceful shutdown and may leave the process running on the node; use only for stuck pods
kubectl delete -f/-k removes everything defined in the manifests, including PVCs (and possibly their data)

name: kubectl edit
notes: Uses $KUBE_EDITOR, then $EDITOR, then vi
Edits are applied to the live object and will be overwritten by the next 'kubectl apply' from your manifests

name: kubectl patch
description: Update specific fields of a resource in place

flags.description: The patch to apply (JSON or YAML)
Patch type: strategic (default), merge, or json
Patch a subresource such as status or scale

examples.description: Change replicas with a strategic merge patch
Replace a value with a JSON patch
Remove finalizers from a stuck resource

notes: Strategic merge patch only works on built-in types; use --type=merge for custom resources
WARNING: removing finalizers skips cleanup logic and can leave orphaned external resources; only do it when you understand why it is stuck
Patched live objects drift from your manifests until you update and re-apply them

name: kubectl diff
description: Show the difference between live objects and local manifests

flags.description: Use server-side apply for the comparison

examples.description: Diff a kustomize overlay against the cluster

notes: Exit code is 0 for no differences, 1 when differences exist, >1 on error, which is handy in CI

name: kubectl kustomize
description: Render a kustomization directory to YAML without applying it

examples.description: Render and apply in one step
Delete everything defined in an overlay

notes: The kustomize bundled with kubectl can lag behind the standalone kustomize CLI
Helm chart inflation needs the --enable-helm flag
WARNING: 'kubectl delete -k' deletes every resource in the overlay

name: kubectl run

examples.description: Run a temporary debug pod that is deleted on exit
Test service connectivity from inside the cluster

notes: Useful for quick debugging
kubectl run only creates pods; use 'kubectl create deployment' for deployments

name: kubectl logs

flags.description: Get logs from all containers in the pod
Prefix each line with its timestamp

examples.description: Follow logs from a pod of a deployment

notes: Use -p to view logs from crashed container

name: kubectl exec
notes: Use -- to separate kubectl args from the command; since kubectl 1.35 the -- is required (the old kubectl exec POD COMMAND form was removed).
Distroless images have no shell; use 'kubectl debug' with an ephemeral container instead

name: kubectl events
description: List cluster events such as scheduling failures, image pull errors and OOM kills

flags.description: Only events for a specific object, e.g. pod/mypod

notes: Events are kept only for a short time (default 1 hour)

name: kubectl debug
description: Debug pods and nodes using ephemeral containers or pod copies

flags.description: Share the process namespace of this container
Create a copy of the pod instead of modifying it
Security profile: general (default), baseline, restricted, netadmin, sysadmin; legacy is deprecated
JSON/YAML file with a partial container spec to customize the profile (e.g. env, securityContext)
With --copy-to, change container images in the copy, e.g. *=busybox

examples.description: Attach a debug shell to a running (e.g. distroless) pod
Copy a pod and start a shell in it, overriding the command
Open a shell on a node (host filesystem at /host)

notes: Ephemeral containers cannot be removed from a pod once added; they exit when you quit the shell
Delete pods created with --copy-to or for node debugging when done
--profile=legacy is deprecated and planned for removal in kubectl 1.39; use general, or sysadmin when you need privileged access.

name: kubectl cp
notes: Requires tar in container

name: kubectl rollout
notes: Works with deployments, daemonsets and statefulsets
See the dedicated status, undo, restart and history entries for details

name: kubectl rollout status
description: Watch a rollout until it completes or fails

flags.description: Give up after this duration, e.g. 5m
Print the current status and exit

examples.description: Wait for a deployment rollout to finish
Fail if the rollout takes longer than 5 minutes (good in CI)

notes: Exits non-zero if the rollout fails or exceeds progressDeadlineSeconds, so it can gate deploy pipelines

name: kubectl rollout restart
description: Restart all pods of a workload with a rolling update

examples.description: Restart all deployments in a namespace

notes: Common after updating a ConfigMap or Secret that pods read at startup
Works by adding a restartedAt annotation to the pod template, so it respects maxUnavailable/maxSurge

name: kubectl rollout undo
description: Roll back a deployment, daemonset, or statefulset to a previous revision

flags.description: Revision to roll back to (default: previous)

examples.description: Roll back to the previous revision

notes: Only the pod template is rolled back; ConfigMaps, Secrets and other resources are not
If you deploy with GitOps or 'kubectl apply', the next sync/apply will undo the rollback; revert in Git instead

name: kubectl rollout history
description: View revision history of a workload

flags.description: Show details of a specific revision

examples.description: Show the pod template of revision 3

examples.command: kubectl annotate deployment/myapp kubernetes.io/change-cause='bump to v2.1'
examples.description: Record a change cause shown in history

notes: The CHANGE-CAUSE column comes from the kubernetes.io/change-cause annotation (the old --record flag is deprecated)
Number of revisions kept is set by spec.revisionHistoryLimit (default 10)

name: kubectl set
notes: Triggers rollout when changing deployment

name: kubectl wait
description: Block until resources reach a condition

flags.description: Condition to wait for: condition=X, delete, jsonpath=..., or create

examples.description: Wait for matching pods to be ready
Wait for a deployment to become available
Wait for a job to finish
Wait for a pod to be deleted
Wait for a field to have a value
Wait for a pod to exist and then become ready (multiple --for conditions are ANDed, kubectl 1.36+)

notes: Fails immediately if no resources match a selector yet; '--for=create' (kubectl 1.31+) waits for creation
A failed Job never becomes Complete; wait with a timeout or also check condition=Failed

name: kubectl config

examples.description: Show only the current context's config

notes: Config file: ~/.kube/config (override with KUBECONFIG, which can list multiple files separated by :)
kubectl config view redacts credentials; add --raw to see them (avoid sharing the output)
User preferences such as aliases and default flags now belong in a separate kuberc file, not kubeconfig (the kubeconfig preferences field is deprecated).

name: kubectl config get-contexts
description: List the contexts (cluster/user/namespace combos) in your kubeconfig

examples.description: List contexts; the current one is marked with *

name: kubectl config use-context
description: Switch kubectl to a different context (cluster)

examples.description: Run a single command against another context without switching

notes: The change is written to your kubeconfig and affects every terminal using it; prefer --context for one-off commands against production
Third-party tools kubectx/kubens make switching faster

name: kubectl config set-context
description: Create or modify a context, e.g. to change its default namespace

flags.description: Cluster and user entries for the context

examples.description: Set the default namespace for the current context

name: kubectl kuberc
description: Configure kubectl aliases and default flags in a kuberc preferences file, separate from kubeconfig.

flags.description: Section to modify: defaults, aliases, or credentialplugin
kubectl command the entry applies to, e.g. get or "set env"
Flag default in the form flag=value (repeatable)

examples.command: kubectl kuberc set --section defaults --command delete --option interactive=true
examples.description: Always ask for confirmation before deleting

examples.command: kubectl kuberc set --section aliases --name getn --command get --prependarg nodes --option output=wide
examples.description: Create an alias so kubectl getn runs kubectl get nodes -o wide

examples.command:
apiVersion: kubectl.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Preference
defaults:
- command: apply
  options:
  - name: server-side
    default: "true"
aliases:
- name: getn
  command: get
  prependArgs:
  - nodes
  options:
  - name: output
    default: wide

examples.description: Run one command with kuberc disabled (for troubleshooting)

notes: kuberc is beta since Kubernetes 1.34 and the kuberc set/view commands are beta since 1.36. The default file is ~/.kube/kuberc; use --kuberc or the KUBERC environment variable for another path.
kuberc can also restrict which exec credential plugins kubectl may run (--section credentialplugin --policy Allowlist).

name: kubectl plugin list
description: List kubectl plugins (executables named kubectl-* on your PATH).

examples.description: Show all plugins kubectl can find and warn about shadowed or non-executable ones
Install the kubectx/kubens plugins via the Krew plugin manager (requires Krew)

notes: Any executable named kubectl-foo on your PATH becomes kubectl foo.
Krew is a separate, community-maintained plugin manager (krew.sigs.k8s.io), not part of kubectl.

name: kubectl create secret
description: Create a Secret from literals, files, or TLS certificates

examples.description: Create a secret from literal values
Create a secret from a .env file
Create a TLS secret for an Ingress

examples.command: kubectl get secret db-creds -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d

notes: Secret data is only base64-encoded, not encrypted; enable encryption at rest and restrict access with RBAC
Literal values end up in shell history; prefer --from-file or --from-env-file
To update an existing secret: add --dry-run=client -o yaml and pipe to 'kubectl apply -f -'

name: kubectl create configmap
description: Create a ConfigMap from literals, files, or env files

examples.description: Create from a file (key is the file name)
Create one key per line of an env file

examples.command: kubectl create configmap app-config --from-file=config/ --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
examples.description: Create or update a configmap from a directory

notes: Pods do not restart automatically when a ConfigMap changes; env vars need a restart (kubectl rollout restart)
Mounted ConfigMap files update eventually, except when mounted with subPath
Size limit is 1 MiB

name: kubectl create token
description: Request a short-lived, bound token for a ServiceAccount (TokenRequest API).

flags.description: Requested lifetime, e.g. 10m or 1h (the server may adjust it)
Bind the token to an object (Pod, Secret, Node) so it is invalidated when the object is deleted

examples.description: Get a token for a ServiceAccount

notes: Since Kubernetes 1.24, ServiceAccounts no longer get long-lived token Secrets automatically; use this command or projected volume tokens instead.
Treat the printed token as a credential; avoid saving it in shell history or logs.

name: kubectl port-forward
notes: Useful for debugging services locally
When forwarding to a service or deployment, kubectl picks one pod; traffic is not load-balanced
The forward stops if the pod restarts; re-run the command
Exposing on 0.0.0.0 makes the port reachable from your network

name: kubectl expose
notes: Creates a service for the resource

name: kubectl scale
notes: Also works with replicasets and statefulsets

name: kubectl autoscale

flags.description: CPU target: a percentage of requests (e.g. 70%) or an average quantity (e.g. 500m) (kubectl 1.34+)
Memory target: a percentage (e.g. 70%) or a quantity (e.g. 200Mi) (kubectl 1.34+)

examples.description: Create an HPA targeting 80% average CPU utilization
Scale on both CPU and memory utilization

notes: Creates an autoscaling/v2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler
Requires metrics-server and resource requests set on the containers
--cpu-percent is deprecated since kubectl 1.34; use --cpu=80% instead

name: kubectl top

examples.description: Find the most memory-hungry pods in the cluster

notes: Requires metrics-server installed

name: kubectl label
notes: Labels are key-value pairs for organization

name: kubectl annotate

examples.command: kubectl annotate pods mypod description="My app"

notes: Annotations store non-identifying metadata

name: kubectl cordon

examples.description: Prevent new pods from being scheduled on a node
Cordon all nodes with a label

notes: Existing pods continue running

name: kubectl uncordon
description: Mark a node as schedulable again

examples.description: Allow new pods on the node after maintenance
Check that STATUS no longer shows SchedulingDisabled

notes: Pods evicted during drain do not move back automatically; new pods will be scheduled here over time

name: kubectl drain

flags.description: Give up after this duration, e.g. 5m
Only evict pods matching a label selector

notes: Evicts pods and cordons node; run 'kubectl uncordon' when maintenance is done
Respects PodDisruptionBudgets, so it can block if a PDB would be violated
WARNING: --delete-emptydir-data discards data in emptyDir volumes, and --force deletes pods not managed by a controller (they won't be recreated)

name: kubectl taint
notes: Effects: NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, NoExecute

name: kubectl cluster-info
description: Show control plane and core service endpoints

examples.description: Show the API server and CoreDNS addresses
Show client and server versions (warns if the skew is outside the supported range)

notes: kubectl supports API servers within one minor version (older or newer) of itself

name: kubectl api-resources

examples.description: Machine-readable list for one API group (-o json/yaml since kubectl 1.34)

notes: Useful for discovering resource types

name: kubectl explain
notes: Great for learning resource schemas

name: kubectl auth can-i
description: Check whether an action is allowed by RBAC

flags.description: Impersonate a user or service account

examples.command: kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n prod
examples.description: Check if you can create deployments in prod

examples.command: kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:myns:my-sa -n myns

examples.description: List everything you can do in a namespace
Show the identity the cluster sees for you

notes: Impersonation with --as requires the 'impersonate' permission
